name: scientific-ml-coldstart-v1
description: General reusable scientific ML priors selected from visible task semantics and visible file names.

spatial_multiomics_domain_identification.title: Spatial multi-omics domain identification
problem_signature: Aligned molecular modalities describe the same spatial observations.
The target is a spatially coherent partition; modality scale, sparsity, and neighborhood geometry dominate.
launch_sequence: Audit shapes, sparsity, preprocessing state, and observation ordering across RNA, ATAC, and coordinates.
Build separate views: PCA/SVD for RNA; TF-IDF plus LSI for raw ATAC, or SVD for already transformed ATAC.
Normalize views separately; compare modality-only, weighted concatenation, and similarity-network fusion.
Add a spatial kNN graph and compare Gaussian-mixture, spectral, and community-detection clustering.
Only after the classical pipeline works, try a shallow graph-attention autoencoder trained from scratch.
cheap_baselines: RNA-only PCA/SVD plus K-means or Gaussian mixture.
ATAC-only LSI/SVD plus the same clustering family.
Coordinates-only spectral clustering and equal-weight fused embeddings.

models.name: PCA/LSI plus spatial graph clustering
instructions: Keep preprocessing separate until after reduction.
Treat molecular-versus-spatial weight as the main early hyperparameter.

models.name: Compact graph-attention autoencoder
instructions: Use fused molecular embeddings as node features and the spatial graph as edges.
Stay shallow until it beats the classical pipeline.

initial_sweep: Molecular/spatial weights 0.0/0.25/0.5/1.0 in a staged, not Cartesian, sweep.
sanity_checks: Rows and observation IDs align across modalities.
No evaluator/test-only metadata enters preprocessing.
All requested domains are nonempty; report modality-only ablations.
resource_notes: Run classical arms on CPU; use sparse matrices and reserve a V100 for the graph model.
failure_pivots: If spatial smoothing collapses domains, reduce spatial weight or use adaptive neighborhoods.
If one modality dominates, whiten/L2-normalize embeddings before retuning fusion.

inverse_protein_folding.title: Inverse protein folding from backbone structure
problem_signature: Protein backbone geometry conditions one amino-acid sequence per structure or designed chain.
Chain mapping, fixed residues, missing atoms, and exact output ordering are common correctness traps.
launch_sequence: Parse structures and chain boundaries; assert residue counts and atom masks before model calls.
Run local ProteinMPNN as the primary prior and sample several low-temperature candidates.
Use local ESM-IF1 as an independent generator/scorer when available; combine within-model ranks rather than raw likelihoods.

If neither specialist checkpoint is available, train a compact geometry-aware message-passing inverse-folding model from scratch on the provided training split using backbone atoms, residue masks, and amino-acid cross-entropy.
Filter by visible validity constraints, preserve fixed residues and exact chain ordering, and keep the best valid generated fallback.
cheap_baselines: ProteinMPNN low-temperature generation with one candidate per structure.
Amino-acid frequency output only as a contract smoke test, never the final arm.

models.name: ProteinMPNN
instructions: Use the local repository entry point and available full-backbone weights.
Batch by length and use scores only after validity checks.

models.name: ESM-IF1
instructions: Load only the local checkpoint.
Use rank aggregation because likelihood scales are not calibrated.

models.name: Compact geometry-aware inverse-folding network
models.role: train-from-scratch fallback when local specialist weights are absent
instructions: Encode N/CA/C/O geometry with invariant distances, orientations, and a shallow message-passing stack.
Use residue masks and teacher-forced amino-acid cross-entropy; keep the model small enough for rapid validation.

models.name: Cross-model candidate rank aggregation
instructions: Deduplicate sequences and combine ranks, validity, and diversity.

initial_sweep: Temperatures 0.10/0.15/0.20; candidates per backbone 4, then 8 or 16 only after validation gains.
Compare ProteinMPNN, ESM-IF1, and rank aggregation before deeper tuning.
Compare available specialist priors against the compact train-from-scratch fallback before deeper tuning.
sanity_checks: Sequence lengths, chain separators, and fixed residues match parsed structures.
No unsupported symbols, empty sequences, NaNs, or chain permutations.
resource_notes: One V100 is enough for the primary models; cache parsed coordinates.
failure_pivots: Missing checkpoint: skip that model and spend budget on more candidates from the available prior.
Valid but poor sequences: audit chain mapping and fixed positions before expanding sweeps.

smlm_point_cloud_clustering.title: Single-molecule localization point-cloud clustering
problem_signature: Unordered 2D/3D localization coordinates have variable density and possible noise points.
Coordinate scaling and neighborhood construction matter more than generic point-cloud pretraining.
launch_sequence: Inspect point counts, physical units, localization uncertainty, and background/noise labels.
Normalize by a robust per-cloud physical or kNN scale without erasing density.
Run DBSCAN, HDBSCAN, and OPTICS-style baselines over a small scale-aware grid.
If supervised labels exist, train a compact EdgeConv/message-passing displacement-to-center network and recluster displaced points.
cheap_baselines: DBSCAN with epsilon derived from kNN distances.
HDBSCAN/OPTICS and connected components on a radius graph.

models.name: Scale-aware density clustering
instructions: Choose parameters relative to local scale.
Track noise and tiny-cluster behavior.

models.name: EdgeConv displacement network
instructions: Predict bounded point displacements.
Use rigid-transform-consistent augmentation and recluster after displacement.

sanity_checks: Invariant to point order and valid rigid transforms.
Handle empty clouds, duplicates, singletons, and noise explicitly.
Reclustering must not collapse the whole cloud.
resource_notes: Density baselines are CPU-friendly; one V100 is enough for the graph network.
failure_pivots: Variable-density failure: use per-cloud scaling or HDBSCAN/OPTICS.
Merged nearby clusters: bound displacement and reduce neighborhood radius.

xray_diffraction_denoising.title: X-ray diffraction intensity denoising
problem_signature: Paired low/high-quality diffraction intensity arrays have heavy-tailed dynamic range.
Narrow scientific peaks must be restored rather than semantically classified or oversmoothed.
launch_sequence: Audit pairing, detector masks, dynamic range, and specimen-level split boundaries.
Establish identity, variance-stabilizing, and small residual U-Net baselines.
Compare log1p and asinh transforms with exact inverse transforms.
Fine-tune one-channel NAFNet when local code/weights exist; use Restormer as a second architecture family, not an immediate ensemble.
Start with L1/Charbonnier, adding a small gradient/structural term only when peak fidelity improves.
cheap_baselines: Variance-stabilizing transform plus a light classical filter.
Small residual U-Net trained from scratch.

models.name: Small residual U-Net
instructions: Use one-channel residual prediction and avoid oversampling blank patches.

models.name: NAFNet
instructions: Adapt input/output layers to one channel while preserving interior weights.
Fine-tune only on locally available paired measured data.

models.name: Restormer
instructions: Check target patch-size memory before a long run.

initial_sweep: One conservative warm-start LR and one 3x smaller.
sanity_checks: Split by original specimen/image before patching.
Outputs are finite, correctly shaped, and nonnegative when required.
Track peak position, width, and integrated intensity in addition to the primary metric.
Beat identity without winning solely by smoothing.
resource_notes: One V100 is sufficient for patch training; use accumulation before multi-GPU complexity.
failure_pivots: Unstable warm start: return to the small U-Net and audit normalization.
Blurred peaks: rebalance peak patches and reduce structural smoothing.

molecular_linker_design.title: Three-dimensional molecular linker design
problem_signature: Two fragments plus attachment atoms/geometry condition a variable-size generated linker.
Chemical validity, exact fragment connectivity, atom mapping, and geometry are hard gates.
Exact source-task implementations are deliberately absent from this general prior.
launch_sequence: Write an RDKit validator first: attachment atoms, atom maps, fragments present exactly once, sanitization, and connectivity.
Fit a visible-data linker-length/attachment-distance prior and make a deterministic reconnection baseline.
Train a compact E(3)-equivariant conditional graph/diffusion model from scratch.
Generate multiple candidates, reject invalid molecules, then rank by task-visible geometry and model score.
Enable any specialist checkpoint arm only when the specialist tier is explicitly selected and the local asset is available.
cheap_baselines: Conditional linker-length predictor plus a small template library.
Split-safe nearest-neighbor retrieval by fragment geometry.

models.name: Compact E(3)-equivariant conditional diffusion model
instructions: Condition on fragments, attachments, relative geometry, and linker length.
Start with a few EGNN-style blocks and a modest diffusion horizon.

models.name: RDKit constrained reconnection baseline
instructions: Guarantee both fragments are present and connected.
Use no external compound service.

models.name: DeLinker
instructions: Use only the local implementation/checkpoint.
Report separately from the general-prior condition.

initial_sweep: Length prior mode vs nearby lengths.
4/6 equivariant blocks, width 128/256 after smoke tests.
50/100 diffusion steps; 16 candidates first, then 64 only if useful.
sanity_checks: RDKit sanitization and exact fragment preservation.
Correct attachments, bond orders, charges, stereochemistry, and atom maps.
Finite coordinates, no catastrophic clashes, no disconnected outputs.
Report validity/connectivity separately from the primary score.
resource_notes: One V100 can train a compact generator; parallelize CPU RDKit checks conservatively.
failure_pivots: Low validity: fix bookkeeping, length conditioning, and sanitization before architecture tuning.
Valid but poor geometry: strengthen relative-coordinate conditioning before adding size.

irregular_temporal_sequence_modeling.title: Temporal sequence modeling with irregular sampling
problem_signature: Measurements arrive at unequal time gaps and may include masks or partially observed channels.
Numerical trajectories, sequential pixels, text tokens, and sensor streams require different routing despite a shared temporal wrapper.
launch_sequence: Inspect tensor semantics, timestamp units/sorting, masks, target horizon, and subtype: numerical, image-derived, text-derived, or sensor/control.
Create explicit delta-time and observation-mask channels; separate padding from true missingness.
Run a standard GRU and GRU-D-style baseline.
For irregular numerical trajectories compare CfC/LTC-style recurrence and Neural CDE; for sequential pixels use compact GRU/CfC; for token text use embedding plus BiGRU/CNN/small Transformer.
Select the family on task-faithful validation, then tune hidden size and LR lightly.
cheap_baselines: Masked summaries plus a linear/tree model.

models.name: GRU-D
instructions: Use masks and time-since-last-observation separately.
Audit zero and very large gaps.

models.name: CfC/LTC-style recurrent model
models.role: continuous-time recurrence for irregular numerical sequences
instructions: Condition updates explicitly on elapsed time.
Compare with GRU-D under the same split.

models.name: Neural CDE
models.role: path model when interpolation semantics fit
instructions: Use split-safe interpolation and account for solver cost.
Do not use for token sequences by reflex.

models.name: Subtype-specific compact sequence model
instructions: Sequential pixels: compact GRU/CfC.
Tokenized text: embedding plus BiGRU/CNN/small Transformer.
Sensor/control: GRU-D, CfC, or Neural CDE.

initial_sweep: GRU/GRU-D/CfC/Neural CDE only where semantically applicable.
Raw time units vs training-set median-gap normalization.
sanity_checks: Sorted finite timestamps with consistent units.
Padding, missing values, and true zeros are distinguishable.
No preprocessing/vocabulary leakage.
Validation preserves target/horizon semantics.
Include a timestamp-ignorant ablation.
resource_notes: Most arms fit on one V100; cap Neural CDE solver cost before increasing model size.
failure_pivots: Continuous-time underperformance: audit time units and subtype suitability.
Overfitting: shrink the model and return to explicit-time GRU rather than adding depth.
